title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 8th District
area: Southern Piedmont North Carolina, including all of Anson, Montgomery, Richmond, Scotland, Stanly, and Union counties and portions of Cabarrus, Mecklenburg, and Robeson counties (Union County/southeast Charlotte suburbs).

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Mark Harris advanced unopposed. Colby Watson won a three-way Democratic primary with 47.9% of the vote.

Harris previously won the Republican nomination for North Carolina's 9th District in 2018, but no candidate was certified as the winner of that November 2018 general election; Harris was elected to the newly numbered 8th District in 2024 after the state's congressional map was redrawn.

summary.text: Mark Harris is the Republican incumbent for North Carolina's 8th Congressional District, a former Baptist pastor with a Ph.D. in Christian leadership who sits on the House Agriculture, Judiciary, and Education and Workforce Committees.

background.text: Born in Winston-Salem, North Carolina; graduated from R.J. Reynolds High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Appalachian State University (1987), and a master's degree in divinity and a Ph.D. in Christian leadership from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary.
Career experience includes working as a pastor; served as a trustee of Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary and on the board of directors of the Biblical Recorder.

Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on the Judiciary (Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust Subcommittee; Constitution and Limited Government Subcommittee), and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.

priorities.text: Wants to reduce regulatory burdens on farmers and champion agricultural policy as a member of the House Agriculture Committee.
priorities.quote: Congressman Harris is committed to advancing policies that reduce regulatory burdens, promote innovation, and empower the agricultural sector.

priorities.text: Supports cutting taxes and regulation for small businesses and opposes new government programs to grow the economy.
priorities.quote: A strong economy starts with free enterprise, low taxes, and hard work—not more government programs.

priorities.text: Wants to return control of education to states and local communities rather than the federal government.
priorities.quote: It's time to return control of education to the states and local communities, as our Founders intended.

positions.summary: Describes himself as committed to protecting the sanctity of life.
positions.quote: As a pastor, Congressman Harris is deeply committed to protecting the sanctity of life and promoting the importance of traditional family values.

positions.summary: Opposes new restrictions on gun rights, describing the right to bear arms as non-negotiable.
positions.quote: The right to bear arms is not negotiable... Congressman Harris remains steadfast in defending Americans' constitutional right to self-defense, resisting any efforts to undermine this fundamental freedom.

positions.summary: Wants education control returned to states and local communities rather than the federal government, reflecting broader support for local/parental control over public funding decisions.
positions.quote: It's time to return control of education to the states and local communities, as our Founders intended.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Agriculture (Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture; Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit), the Committee on the Judiciary, and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Colby Watson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 47.9% of the vote over two challengers.

summary.text: Colby Watson is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 8th Congressional District, a small business owner from Indian Trail running on ending money in politics and lowering the cost of living.

background.text: Born in Indian Trail, North Carolina, part of the 8th District; earned a high school diploma through homeschooling.
Career experience includes working as a small business owner.

priorities.text: Wants to end the influence of super PACs and corporate lobbyists in politics.
priorities.quote: Our democracy has been hijacked by big money and special interests. I'm running to restore power to the people by ending the influence of super PACs and corporate lobbyists.

priorities.text: Wants to address the cost-of-living crisis and growing wealth inequality by investing in communities, schools, healthcare, and infrastructure.
priorities.quote: The cost of living keeps rising while wages stay the same, forcing working families to do more with less.

positions.summary: Says prosperity should not be reserved for those at the top and wants Congress to prioritize the middle class over the wealthy in tax and spending decisions.
positions.quote: If elected, I would use that power to prioritize the middle class, working families, and small businesses, not the wealthy and well-connected.

positions.summary: Points to families being repeatedly outbid by investment firms when trying to buy a first home as a problem needing a legislative response.
positions.quote: Working families should never have to compete with corporate investors just to have a place to call home.

summary.text: Bo Whitehead is the Green Party candidate for North Carolina's 8th Congressional District.
